newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian Airlines says 1996 profit, revenue up.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian Airlines says 1996 profit, revenue up.

text.p: State-run Lithuanian Airlines said on Friday that its profit before taxes in 1996 was 8.7 million litas versus a loss of 2.3 million litas in 1995.
The company, which has been put on the privatisation list, said in a statement that its 1996 revenue reached 183.7 million litas, up from 170.2 million litas the previous year.
The company said that it had 4,450 flights in 1996 compared to 4,218 in 1995.
It said it carried 183,300 passengers in 1996 compared with 175,800 in 1995 and transported 1,448 tonnes of cargo versus 1,198 tonnes in 1995.
Lithuanian Airlines has a fleet of 11 Russian made Yak-42s, three Boeing 737-200s, and one SAAB -340. One of the Boeings and the SAAB are leased.
The company plans to sell all of its Yaks before the end of this year and to lease another SAAB-340 in April or May.
The Lithuanian government said earlier this month that it planned to sell part of its stake in the airline but intended to retain control of 51 percent of the shares.
The airlines of both neighbouring Baltic states Estonia and Latvia have already been sold.
Scandinavian Airlines owns a big stake in Latvia's Air Baltic while Danish Maersk, part of A.P. Moeller, owns a majority stake in Estonian Air.
